newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice export prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice export prices seen mixed.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are expected to remain mixed next week as exporters plan to clinch deals before the end of the current financial year on June 30, dealers said on Thursday.
Some exporters were negotiating deals with importers in the Gulf and Africa for exports before June 30, one dealer said.

An official of the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) said the corporation had received three bids on Monday for the sale and export of 5,000 tonnes of basmati variety Pak-7 rice containing seven percent broken.
But no decision had been taken on the bids that were quoted at $436, $435.10 and $425 per tonne FOB.
The dealer said IRRI-6 prices were likely to firm due to a demand from African countries but basmati prices were likely to remain stable.
Pakistan exported 1.571 million tonnes of rice worth $393 million in the first 10 months to April of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) against 1.133 million worth $372 million in the same period a year ago.
In April, rice exports fell to 180,094 tonnes worth $48 million compared with 372,828 tonnes worth $62 million in March and 118,141 tonnes worth $38 million in April 1996.
